1.note: David is speaking of his earnest prayer and worship as if he were to physically **lift up** his **soul** to Yahweh. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I pour out my heart] or [I come in prayer]

2.note: David is not using the phrase **My God** to mean that he is the only one who worships Yahweh nor that he possesses or controls Yahweh. Rather he uses these words to emphasize that Yahweh is the God that he worships. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [You God, whom I worship,]

David is using imperative forms, **do not let me be ashamed** and **do not let my enemies exult over me**, but he intends these as polite requests rather than commands. If the imperative forms do not communicate polite requests in your language, you could use forms that communicate polite requests. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [please do not let me have shame; please do not let my enemies exult over me]

3.note: By **the ones waiting on you**, David means people who trust in Yahweh and depend on him for help. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [all those who trust in you] or [all the ones trusting in you]

David is using a double negative that consists of **not** and the negative meaning contained in the word **ashamed**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [all the ones waiting on you, you will help]

4.note: These are imperatives, but they communicate polite requests rather than commands. If the imperative forms do not communicate polite requests for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates polite requests. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please make me know your ways, Yahweh; please teach me your paths]

These two phrases **Make me know your ways, Yahweh** and **teach me your paths** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [Make me know your ways, Yahweh, yes, teach me your paths]

David is speaking of how to live as if it were **paths** that he could walk along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [teach me how to live according to your will] or [teach me how I should live]

5.note: David is speaking of God’s **truth** as if it were a path that he could walk on. He means that he wants God to help him live according to God’s truth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Help me to live according to your truth]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **truth**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Lead me according to what is true] or [Lead me by your true teaching]

The expressions **Lead me in your truth** and **teach me** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Instruct me in your truth]

The verbs **Lead** and **teach** are imperatives, but they communicate polite requests rather than commands. David is humbly asking God to guide and instruct him. If the imperative form does not communicate a polite request in your language, you could use a form that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please lead me in your truth and teach me]
See how you translated the similar phrase “the God of his salvation” in 24:5.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for you are the God who saves me]

The implication is that David waits on God to help him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I continually wait for you to help me] or [I wait on you to help me all the day]

6.note: David assumes that readers will know that when he asks God to **Remember** his compassion and covenant faithfulness, he is asking God to act according to these qualities, not simply to recall them mentally. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Act according to your compassion, Yahweh, and your covenant faithfulness]

The word translated as **Remember** is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please remember your compassion, Yahweh, and your covenant faithfulness]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **compassion** and **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [Remember how you are compassionate, Yahweh, and how you are faithful to your covenant] or [Remember to be compassionate, Yahweh, and to be faithful to your covenant]

The implication is that God has always been compassionate and faithful, not just recently. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [you have acted with compassion and covenant faithfulness since ancient times]

7.note: David is using the possessive form to describe **sins** that were committed during his **youth**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the sins I committed when I was young] or [the sinful things I did in my youth]

By **according to your covenant faithfulness remember me**, David means that he wants God to remember him with favor and blessing, not with judgment. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [because of your covenant faithfulness remember me]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **transgressions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [or the ways I have disobeyed your instructions]
See how you translated the phrase **covenant faithfulness** in the previous verse.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **goodness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for the sake of the fact that you are good, Yahweh]

8.q: טוֹב־וְ⁠יָשָׁ֥ר יְהוָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֤ן יוֹרֶ֖ה חַטָּאִ֣ים בַּ⁠דָּֽרֶךְ
8.note: David is using **therefore** to introduce a result clause that explains what follows from Yahweh being good and upright. If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because Yahweh teaches sinners the way, he is good and upright]

David is using the adjective **sinful** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [sinners]

Here David is speaking of how a person lives as if that were a **way** or path for a person to walk on. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [how to live] or [how they should conduct their lives]

9.q: יַדְרֵ֣ךְ עֲ֭נָוִים בַּ⁠מִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וִֽ⁠ילַמֵּ֖ד עֲנָוִ֣ים דַּרְכּֽ⁠וֹ
9.note: David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a guide who **leads** people along paths and a teacher who **teaches** them the right way to take. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [He guides the humble to do what is just and he shows the humble how he wants them to live]

9.q: יַדְרֵ֣ךְ עֲ֭נָוִים בַּ⁠מִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וִֽ⁠ילַמֵּ֖ד עֲנָוִ֣ים דַּרְכּֽ⁠וֹ
9.note: David is using the adjective **humble** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [He leads humble people in justice and he teaches humble people his way]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [He leads the humble to do what is just] or [He guides the humble to act justly]

10.note: Here David is speaking of Yahweh’s actions as if they were **paths** that a person could walk along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All the actions of Yahweh are covenant love and faithfulness]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant love** and **faithfulness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [All the paths of Yahweh are loving and faithful]

11.note: David is using the term **name** to represent who Yahweh is or to refer to Yahweh’s reputation. Alternate translation: [For your sake] or [For the sake of your reputation]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [forgive me for the wrong things I have done]

12.q: מִי־זֶ֣ה הָ֭⁠אִישׁ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה י֝וֹרֶ֗⁠נּוּ בְּ⁠דֶ֣רֶךְ יִבְחָֽר
12.note: David is using a rhetorical question **Who is the man fearing Yahweh?** to emphasize that God is faithful to guide those who revere him. If a speaker of your language would not use a question for this purpose, you could translate this as a statement or exclamation. Alternate translation: [The man who fears Yahweh—God will teach him in the way he is to choose]

12.q: מִי־זֶ֣ה הָ֭⁠אִישׁ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה י֝וֹרֶ֗⁠נּוּ בְּ⁠דֶ֣רֶךְ יִבְחָֽר
12.note: The psalmist is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Who are the people fearing Yahweh? He will teach them in the way they are to choose]

The psalmist is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [anyone]

David is speaking of how a person conducts themselves as if that were **the way** or path for a person to walk on. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [He will teach him how he should live]

13.note: David is using the term **soul** to mean the entire person from the perspective of his spiritual and emotional existence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [He]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **good**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [His soul will remain prosperous] or [He will continue to be blessed]

By **in good**, David means in prosperity or in favorable circumstances. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in prosperity]
See how you translated the term “seed” in 18:50. Alternate translation: [and his descendants]

By **will inherit the earth**, David means that their descendants will continue to live in the promised land of Israel. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [will inherit the land]

14.note: David assumes that readers will know that **the secret of Yahweh** refers to an intimate relationship with Yahweh. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s intimate friendship is for the ones fearing him] or [Yahweh shares his plans with the ones fearing him]

15.q: עֵינַ֣⁠י תָּ֭מִיד אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י הֽוּא־יוֹצִ֖יא מֵ⁠רֶ֣שֶׁת רַגְלָֽ⁠י
15.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because Yahweh will make my feet go out of the net, my eyes are continually toward him]

Here, **eyes** represents David’s attention and focus. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am continually focused on Yahweh]

Here David is speaking as if his troubles were a **net** that had trapped his feet and as if Yahweh could free his feet from that trap. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this as a comparison or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will free me from my troubles like feet freed from a net] or [he will rescue me from my troubles]

16.note: David is using imperative forms, but he is communicating polite requests rather than commands. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please turn toward me and be gracious to me]

Here David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a person who could physically **Turn toward** him to give attention. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Pay attention to me]

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because I am alone and afflicted, turn toward me and be gracious to me]

The expression **afflicted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and experiencing hardship]

17.note: Here David is speaking of **The troubles of my heart** as if they were physical objects that could become larger in size. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My heart is filled with many troubles] or [The troubles I feel have become very great]

Here David is speaking as if his distresses were a place from which he could be brought **out**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [free me from my distresses] or [rescue me from my distresses]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **distresses**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [deliver me from the things that distress me] or [bring me out of the circumstances that distress me]

18.note: By **See**, David means “take notice of” or “pay attention to.” David is asking God to consider his difficult situation with compassion. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Consider]

The words **See** and **forgive** are imperatives, but they communicate polite requests rather than commands. If the imperative form does not communicate polite requests in your language, you could use a form that communicates polite requests. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please see my affliction and my trouble, and please forgive all of my sins]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **affliction** and **trouble**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [See how I am afflicted and troubled, and forgive all of the sinful things that I have done]

19.note: This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please look at] or [Please consider]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **hatred**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and they violently hate me]

David is using this possessive form **hatred of violence** to mean violent hatred. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and with violent hatred] or [and with brutal hatred]

20.note: These are imperatives, but they communicate polite requests rather than commands. If the imperatives do not communicate polite requests for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates polite requests. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please guard my life and deliver me; please do not let me have shame]

By **Guard my life**, David means protect him from his enemies who want to harm or kill him. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Protect my life]
See how you translated the phrase **for I take refuge in you** in 16:1.

21.note: The terms **integrity** and **uprightness** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [May complete righteousness]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **integrity** and **uprightness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [May my honest and upright character preserve me] or [May I be preserved because I am honest and do what is right]

Here David speaks of **integrity and uprightness** as if they were people who could **preserve** or protect him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [May my integrity and uprightness be the means by which you preserve me]

See how you translated the phrases “the ones waiting on you” in 25:3 and “on you I wait” in 25:5 where the words “waiting” and “wait” are used with the same meaning as the word **wait** in this verse.

22.note: The word **redeem** is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [please redeem]

Here, **Israel** represents the Israelite people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [us Israelite people from all our troubles]
